Class RouteLocator

java.lang.Object
io.micronaut.web.router.RouteLocator
@Internal public final class RouteLocator extends Object
The target of a locator route, see HttpRouteScope.locate(String, LocatorHandler, Function). The route matches its prefix followed by the rest of the path, for every standard HTTP method. When the router selects it, the router runs the locator and matches the rest of the path with the routes of the RouteTable of the LocatedRoutes of the located target, and answers the route of that table, with the path variables of both and the target, instead of the locator route. The table may have locator routes too, which locate again. The table of a LocatedRoutes is built by the RouteTableFactory of the routes, on the first target it routes.
Since:
5.3.0
Author:
Denis Stepanov

    • isLocating

      public static boolean isLocating(HttpRequest<?> request)
      Whether an asynchronous locator has not located its target for the request yet: until it has, the router does not know the routes of the target, e.g. for Router.findAny(HttpRequest). Matching the request with Router.findClosest(HttpRequest) waits for it, see pendingLocation(Throwable).
      Parameters:
      request - The request
      Returns:
      Whether a locator of the request is still locating its target
      Since:
      5.3.0

    • cancelPendingLocations

      public static void cancelPendingLocations(HttpRequest<?> request)
      Cancel the asynchronous locators that have not located their targets for the request yet, e.g. when the client went away: the stage each of them returned is cancelled, and matching the request fails with a CancellationException instead of waiting for the target.
      Parameters:
      request - The request
      Since:
      5.3.0
